## Summary

Two refactorings applied to `src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math3/util/FastMath.java`:

1. **`Split(double, double)` constructor** — replaced the unreadable nested ternary expression `high == 0.0 ? (low == 0.0 && Double.doubleToRawLongBits(high) == Long.MIN_VALUE ? -0.0 : low) : high + low` with a named static helper `combineSplit(high, low)` that uses straightforward `if` statements. The signed-zero edge case (preserving `-0.0` when both parts are zero) is now explicit and documented.

2. **`pow(double, double)` outer `else`** — the entire ~130-line method body lived inside `if (y == 0) { return 1.0; } else { ... }`. Replaced with an early return, eliminating one indentation level for the whole method and removing the redundant `result` temporary at the end of the general-case path.

No public API, method signatures, numerical behavior, or dependencies were changed. Skipped a candidate extraction of the `PI/2 - (xa, xb)` block shared by `cosQ` and `tan` because it would either allocate a fresh `double[]` in hot trig paths or force the call sites to materialize an out-parameter buffer they don't otherwise need.

Both FastMath test suites pass unchanged (`FastMathTest`: 71 tests, `FastMathStrictComparisonTest`: 66 tests, 0 failures).
